ENGLISH — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goed
   C. goes
   D. going

3. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.

4. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the Library

5. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

7. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.

8. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a joining word
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only an action

9. When practising Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.

10. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. quickly
   C. blue
   D. happiness

11. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

12. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

13. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

14. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

15. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. No full stops
